title: Broken subtitles mix languages and timestamps when casting to Chromecast
body: After upgrading Jellyfin Server from 10.8.13-1 to 10.9.x, subtitles became broken when casting from the Android client to Chromecast. Playback starts normally, but subtitles from different language tracks and unrelated timestamps soon appear alternately or overlaid. The same movies work in a browser and the Android web player. This mainly affects movies with multiple large external SRT tracks. Enabling or disabling on-the-fly subtitle extraction does not fix it, and failures strongly correlate with server log messages such as `errors encountered while parsing 'srt' subtitle using the SubRip format parser`. My server runs directly on Debian Bookworm with jellyfin-ffmpeg6, Intel QSV, no plugins, and no reverse proxy.

symptoms_visible: When I cast from Android to Chromecast, the first subtitles may look normal, but lines from different languages and unrelated timestamps soon alternate or overlap and become unreadable.
The same movies and subtitle tracks display correctly in a browser and in the Android web player.
N0.label: N0 mixed Chromecast subtitles reported

symptoms_visible: The Chromecast still plays lines from several subtitle tracks at once, although the individual cached SRT files each contain only one language.
Media with only one subtitle track does not show the same mixing.
N1.label: N1 source subtitle files checked

symptoms_visible: After upgrading to the server release containing the newer libse package, the same media still produces mixed-language subtitles and the same parser errors.
N2_x.label: N2_x libse-only update aftermath

symptoms_visible: The installed server still mixes subtitle tracks, but all previously affected media display subtitles correctly with the experimental build where subtitle formats are obtained inside each Parse call.
N3.label: N3 fresh-format-instance experiment succeeds

symptoms_visible: On an affected setup updated to a build containing the fix, Chromecast playback shows only the selected subtitle language at the correct timestamps.
N_terminal.label: terminal fixed on affected setup

question_patterns: Can you inspect the extracted SRT files in the Jellyfin subtitle cache and tell me whether an individual file already contains mixed languages?
Are the cached subtitle files themselves corrupted, or does each file contain one normal language track?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I checked several SRT files in the subtitle cache. They look reasonable, and each file contains subtitles in only one language. It looks like several separate tracks are being played together rather than one file already containing mixed languages.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Each cached SRT file already contains lines from several languages and unrelated timestamps.
I checked a larger sample and every cached file still contains only its own language.

edges.comment: Real thread c30-c35: participant4 requested inspection of the subtitle cache; affected participants 10 and 7 reported that individual SRT files looked correct and that single-track media was unaffected. These affected users are folded into the simulated user side; the evidence concerns their own affected Jellyfin deployments.

solution.intent: Treat the bug as a libse package-version defect and update Jellyfin to a release containing a newer libse version.
solution.concrete_example: Upgrade to the Jellyfin release containing the libse 4.0.7 bump and retry the same media.

edges.comment: Real thread c13-c18: participant5 initially reported success after changing libse versions, but the reporter upgraded to 10.9.9 with the bump and observed exactly the same symptoms and errors. Participant5 then withdrew the earlier conclusion. The reporter kept the upgraded server, so the persistent state changes from S1 to S2.

question_patterns: Could you test the proposed experimental server build against media that reliably showed the problem and report what appears on screen?
Please try the candidate parser change on several previously affected files and tell me whether the subtitle tracks still become mixed.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I changed the Parse function to call GetSubtitleFormats() inside the function and tested it. From what I can tell, it fixes the issue: all the media that had problems before now displays the subtitles correctly.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The experimental build still mixes languages on the same affected media.
The experimental build works on all of my previously affected files, but I have only tested one Chromecast device.

edges.comment: Real thread c36-c40: participant4 hypothesized unsafe reuse of SubtitleFormat instances, participant10 suggested constructing formats in Parse, and affected participant13 built and tested that experiment successfully. The test build is treated as a throwaway pre-landing measurement on another affected deployment folded into the user side; it does not change the retained S2 installation.

solution.intent: Stop sharing cached SubtitleFormat instances between concurrent subtitle parses: cache format types if desired, but construct a fresh format instance for each Parse call, then have affected users verify a build containing the change.
solution.concrete_example: Replace the cache of reusable SubtitleFormat objects with a cache of format types and instantiate the selected format inside each Parse call. Ask an affected user to retest previously failing multi-track media on a build containing that change before declaring the issue resolved.
solution.inference_hint: The user-facing experiment establishes that constructing subtitle format objects inside Parse prevents the failure. The maintainer-side conclusion is that cached SubtitleFormat instances carry state and are unsafe to reuse across concurrent Parse calls; the production refinement caches format classes/types and creates one new instance per call.

edges.comment: Real thread c36-c46: the successful proof of concept was refined to cache format types rather than instances, the maintainer opened the fix, and affected participant14 confirmed correct behavior after installing the landed build. This final confirmation is from a different affected operator, not the original reporter, and is explicitly folded into the simulated user side. It is terminal-side verification and is not required evidence for proposing the fix.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted root cause: Jellyfin reused cached, stateful SubtitleFormat instances across subtitle Parse calls, allowing concurrent parsing state to mix subtitle tracks.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the clean per-language cached SRT files, correlated parser errors, and the successful experimental build that constructs formats inside Parse.
The fix must create a fresh SubtitleFormat instance for each Parse call; caching format types or classes is acceptable, but sharing parser instances is not.

Must not present changing the libse package version as the complete fix, because both the rollback and upgrade conclusions were withdrawn and the reporter reproduced the issue after the newer version shipped.
Must not present toggling on-the-fly extraction or rebuilding the subtitle cache as a reliable fix, because those approaches were reported to have no effect or only temporary improvement.
Must ask an affected user to verify previously failing multi-track media on a build containing the parser-instance fix before treating the issue as resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Jellyfin administrator who can read debug logs, inspect subtitle cache files, modify subtitle encodings, test custom server builds, and discuss source code, but initially lacks familiarity with Jellyfin's internal architecture. Evidence from several similarly technical affected users is folded into the user side.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, investigative, and cooperative; supplies logs and controlled experiments, clearly marks uncertainty, and corrects earlier conclusions when later testing contradicts them.
